meanings.note: Definite article agreeing in gender and number with its noun; also common before given names in casual Brazilian speech.

examples.trans: What is your job title?
Look at the young woman over there.

meanings.note: Alone as vocative gente! it means folks/guys; with article a gente it means we/us with third-person singular verbs.

examples.text: Você acha que é melhor que a gente?
examples.trans: Do you think you're better than us?
Oh, folks, the meeting ran late.

meanings.note: Followed directly by an infinitive without a preposition.

examples.text: A gente não conseguiu encaixar direito.
examples.trans: We could not manage to fit it in right.
Did you manage to sort it out?

meanings.note: Verbs in -ear take -ei- in rhizotonic present forms and -eei in 1st sg past (mapeei).

examples.text: A gente conseguiu mapear a placa.
examples.trans: We managed to map the board.

examples.text: Fui eu que mapeei o circuito.
examples.trans: I am the one who mapped the circuit.

meanings.note: Here, the electronic circuit board inside the device.

examples.text: A gente conseguiu mapear a placa.
examples.trans: We managed to map the circuit board.
They replaced the computer board.

meanings.note: Electrical path on a board or device.

examples.trans: The circuit is asymmetrical.
Let's not polarize the circuit.

meanings.note: Used for identifying a type of meeting or the department a person belongs to. The present forms sou and é are irregular.

examples.trans: I’m in finance.
It’s a marketing meeting.

meanings.note: Not symmetrical or balanced.

examples.trans: The circuit is asymmetrical.

examples.text: A peça tem um formato assimétrico.
examples.trans: The part has an asymmetrical shape.

meanings.note: Coordinating conjunction pronounced [i] in natural Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Ela faltou e adiantou o trabalho.
examples.trans: She missed it and got ahead on her work.
There are good and bad numbers.

meanings.note: Electrically operated switch inside a circuit.

examples.text: O relé está invertido na placa.
examples.trans: The relay is inverted on the board.
We need to test the relay.

meanings.note: Used here for being present at an event. Vou estar keeps estar in the infinitive after the finite form vou.

examples.trans: I’m not going to be at that meeting.
Are you going to be at that meeting?

meanings.note: Turned upside down or wired backward.

examples.trans: The relay is inverted.
The colors are reversed.

meanings.note: É o seguinte is a very common spoken opener meaning here is the deal.

examples.text: É o seguinte, você precisa cortar o fio.
examples.trans: Here is the thing, you need to cut the wire.
On the following day, everything changed.

meanings.note: A person being addressed, with third-person verb agreement: você vai, vocês vão. Vai and vão are forms of ir, not forms of the pronoun. Common in Brazil; not a rule that every Brazilian region uses the same address system.

examples.trans: Are you going to the meeting?
Are you in finance?

meanings.note: Takes de before a noun (precisa da ajuda) and links directly to an infinitive (precisava gritar).

examples.text: Ela precisa da ajuda do colega.
examples.trans: She needs her colleague's help.
Did you need to shout at me?

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Você precisa cortar o fio verde.
examples.trans: You need to cut the green wire.
Cut that wire right now!

meanings.note: Electrical wire or strand; fio terra is a ground wire.

examples.text: Você precisa cortar o fio certo.
examples.trans: You need to cut the right wire.
Cut the ground wire right away.

meanings.note: Color of grass and the main field of Brazil's flag.

examples.text: Corta o fio verde e amarelo.
examples.trans: Cut the green and yellow wire.
The light is already green.

meanings.note: Color of gold or ripe lemons; paired with verde for Brazil's flag colors.

examples.text: Você precisa cortar o fio verde e amarelo.
examples.trans: You need to cut the green and yellow wire.
She bought a yellow shirt.

meanings.note: 1st sg present repito is used over the radio like English 'I repeat'.

examples.trans: I repeat, cut the green wire.
Can you repeat the address?

meanings.note: Used for taking transport, grabbing items, or taking an apartment first.

examples.trans: They will grab it ahead of me.
I do not need to take the subway.

meanings.note: Used standalone as an incredulous question: Sério? (Seriously?).

examples.trans: Seriously, folks? Green and yellow?
This matter is very serious.

meanings.note: Introduces a contrast. The informal thanks softens the refusal; it does not accept the invitation.

examples.trans: I’m not going, but thanks.
It’s a meeting, but I’m not going.

meanings.note: All-purpose connector, relative link, question opener, and comparative word after mais or melhor.

examples.text: Eu acho que ele já foi.
examples.trans: I think that he already left.
What is this, man?

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner; in spoken Brazilian Portuguese esse commonly covers both this near me and that just mentioned.

examples.text: Esse slide aqui eu fiz ontem.
examples.trans: This slide here I made yesterday.

examples.text: Vou ficar sentado esse tempo inteiro.
examples.trans: I'm going to stay seated that whole time.

meanings.note: Color of rubies or danger wires; also associated with left-wing politics.

examples.trans: This red wire is inactive.
Our wiring will never be red!

meanings.note: Points to the speaker's location or reinforces demonstratives like isso aqui and esse slide aqui.

examples.text: Ela veio aqui olhar um extintor.
examples.trans: She came here to check an extinguisher.
This here is a chart.

meanings.note: First-person singular object clitic.

examples.trans: Would you help me real quick?

examples.text: Por favor, me deixa morar aqui!
examples.trans: Please let me live here!

meanings.note: In the passive ser chamado, means to be called by a label.

examples.text: A gente não gosta de ser chamada assim.
examples.trans: We do not like to be called that.
What is your name?

meanings.note: Used in chamar a atenção (to catch someone's eye) and as an announcement call.

examples.text: Esse fio está me chamando a atenção.
examples.trans: This wire is catching my attention.
Attention, ladies and gentlemen!

meanings.note: A negative answer or a negation in a sentence. A final repeated não can reinforce a conversational refusal in Brazil.

examples.trans: No, I’m not going.
Aren’t you going?

meanings.note: Agrees with its noun as a determiner/adjective; singular muita coisa idiomatically means many things.

examples.trans: They say a lot of things.
I have many numbers here.

meanings.note: Drastic or politically extreme.

examples.text: Não é muito radical cortar agora?
examples.trans: Isn't it too radical to cut right now?
It was a radical change.

meanings.note: Marks the current moment resulting from an earlier action.

examples.trans: Now she is in a meeting.

examples.text: Agora tenho que resolver umas coisinhas.
examples.trans: Right now I have to sort out a few little things.

meanings.note: Device that triggers an explosive charge.

examples.text: O vermelho está ligado no detonador.
examples.trans: The red one is connected to the detonator.
The detonator draws power directly.

meanings.note: Despite looking like English push, puxar means to pull or draw (power).

examples.trans: The detonator is drawing power.
Pull the door to come in.

meanings.note: Electrical power or physical vitality.

examples.trans: The device is drawing power.
We are out of electrical power.

meanings.note: Often used adverbially in speech to mean straight or nonstop.

examples.text: O aparelho puxa energia direto pra ele.
examples.trans: The device draws power straight to it.
We took a direct flight.

meanings.note: Informal reduced para. Before a feminine noun, this Brazilian spelling can also represent a contraction including the article a; the exact meeting is clear from context.

examples.trans: I’m going to the meeting.
Are you going to the meeting?

meanings.note: Third-person masculine singular subject pronoun.

examples.trans: He isn't coming anymore.
He canceled the meeting.

meanings.note: Expresses duration (por uma hora) and fixed phrases like por exemplo.

examples.trans: I stayed there for an hour.
Look at her, for example.

meanings.note: In por favor, the standard polite 'please'.

examples.text: Ei, por favor, não desliga, não!
examples.trans: Hey, please do not hang up!
Can you do me a favor?

meanings.note: In the farewell até logo it anticipates meeting again. This is the time adverb, not a short form for a company logo.

examples.trans: See you later!
I’ll go to the meeting soon.

meanings.note: Used standalone or as calma aí! to tell someone to slow down and relax.

examples.trans: Easy, that's not it!
Hang on, I'm coming.

meanings.note: Adds immediacy after imperatives like calma aí, or means there near you.

examples.trans: Hang on!
Who is there?

meanings.note: Adds another person or item to what was already stated.

examples.trans: I want you to go in too.
I'm the one who made it too!

meanings.note: Vou + infinitive can express a future intention: vou estar means I am going to be. Você takes the third-person vai.

examples.trans: I’m going to the meeting.
Aren’t you going?

meanings.note: Used with a double meaning: electrical polarization and political polarization.

examples.trans: Let's not polarize the circuit.

examples.text: O debate acabou polarizando a sala.
examples.trans: The debate ended up polarizing the room.

meanings.note: Everyday adjective in tá bom (okay), boa tarde (good afternoon), and Bom, pessoal (Well, folks).

examples.trans: All right, I'll go.
Some numbers are good.

meanings.note: First-person plural possessive agreeing in gender and number with the noun.

examples.text: Ela está com a nossa equipe.
examples.trans: She is with our team.
Our work ran late.

meanings.note: Core foundation or support of a system.

examples.text: O verde e amarelo é nossa base.
examples.trans: The green and yellow is our foundation.

examples.text: Essa é a base do projeto.
examples.trans: This is the foundation of the project.

meanings.note: Underlying framework that holds something together.

examples.trans: It is our structure.

examples.text: A estrutura do prédio é forte.
examples.trans: The building's structure is strong.

meanings.note: In até logo it looks ahead to the next meeting. The phrase is added as the lesson farewell, not quoted from the selected source window.

examples.trans: See you later!
See you later. Thanks!
